title: Goulash
subtitle: Hungarian beef and paprika stew
excerpt: Beef and onions slow-cooked in a rich sauce built almost entirely on sweet Hungarian paprika and caraway seeds. Served with egg noodles or mashed potato and a spoonful of soured cream.

recipe.sourceNotes: Goulash (gulyás) is the national dish of Hungary, originally a herdsmen's stew made with dried beef and onions cooked over an open fire. The defining ingredient is paprika: Hungary became the centre of European paprika production after the Ottomans introduced the pepper in the 16th century. Hungarian sweet paprika has a distinctly sweet, fruity character different from Spanish smoked paprika. The dish came to Britain via Central European Jewish cooking and post-war immigration, and became a British cookbook staple by the 1960s.

recipeTools.notes: Or a heavy casserole dish with a lid.

content.text: The paprika is the soul of this dish: use a good-quality sweet Hungarian paprika and use it generously. Add it to the softened onions off the heat to protect it from burning: paprika scorches very quickly and turns bitter. The stew needs a minimum of 1.5 hours to develop its full flavour; 2 hours gives a better result.
Heat the oil in a large, heavy-based pot over high heat. Brown the beef in batches until coloured on all sides. Set aside. Reduce the heat to medium.

Fry the onion in the same pot for 10 minutes until very soft and golden. Add the garlic, red pepper, and caraway seeds. Cook for 3 minutes. Remove from the heat. Stir in the paprika and tomato paste. Return to low heat for 1 minute.

Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, and browned beef. Season. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook over very low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours until the beef is completely tender. Serve with egg noodles or mashed potato, topped with soured cream and parsley.
